table.title: [adversarial] Long headers over tiny numbers
table.md:
| Site | Average weekly active users across all platforms | Median session length in minutes | Share of sessions that ended in a purchase | Number of support tickets opened |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| A | 12k | 7.1 | 3.2% | 41 |
| B | 9.8k | 6.4 | 2.9% | 37 |
| C | 4.1k | 9.0 | 4.4% | 12 |

understanding.purpose: Compare site activity, session duration, purchase conversion and support demand across three sites.
understanding.reading: Read each row as a site profile and scan down each metric to compare sites; the long headers will determine header height while the short body values leave ample space.
groups: Columns 2 and 3 describe activity and engagement; column 4 describes conversion; column 5 describes support demand. All four are comparable site metrics, while column 1 identifies each row.
keep_intact: Site identifiers A, B and C
may_wrap: The four metric headers can wrap at spaces; their shared header row can absorb multiple lines.

preferred.name: r3A
preferred.note: Combine r2A’s more natural activity wrap with r2C’s improved session wrap. Take the needed space from support, whose header already occupies four lines, and check whether it remains readable at the narrower width.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Move width from the shorter session header to activity and conversion, while keeping support wide enough for natural phrases. This refines the balanced rhythm of r0A.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Give the longest header more room while preserving usable widths for the other metrics; test whether activity can wrap more naturally without creating a new bottleneck.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Favor the long conversion header while retaining more width for activity and support than in the uneven earlier designs.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Shift a little width from support to activity relative to r1A, testing whether the activity header can form a more compact shape while keeping the metrics reasonably balanced.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Refine r1C by giving duration and activity slightly more room while retaining most of the conversion column’s advantage. Check whether conversion and support keep their coherent wrapping.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Try a wider duration column to reduce its narrow stacked appearance, accepting tighter conversion and support headers in exchange.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Keep the improved session width and restore r2B’s three-line purchase header. Test whether the activity and support headers remain balanced with the remaining space.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The median and support columns have less text width than their longest words require, forcing words to split. The wide neighboring columns also make the distribution feel uneven.
bad.why: The median and support columns have less text width than their longest words require, forcing words to split. The wide neighboring columns also make the distribution feel uneven.

rationale: r3A gives the two longest headers enough room to form relatively coherent phrases while keeping the median header to three lines. The support header is narrow but remains legible without splitting words, and the short values are easy to scan down their columns. The compact Site column leaves space for the descriptive measures.

general: Allocate width to support meaningful header phrases as well as intact body values.
Columns serving similar roles should have a comfortable visual rhythm, though their widths can differ to accommodate their content.
specific: The tiny numeric values need little width; the long headers determine the allocation here.
All eight candidates fit the viewport and keep words intact, so their differences are matters of wrapping and proportion rather than basic usability.

tradeoffs: r3B gives the purchase header a more compact three-line wrap, but the active-users header then takes four lines. r2C gives the support column more breathing room at the cost of a four-line active-users header.
uncertain: The ranges are approximate visual tolerances, not tested guarantees. They assume the other columns adjust proportionally to keep the total within 592px; wrapping can change abruptly at individual pixel thresholds.

critique.good: The four metric columns have a steady rhythm, and the three site rows are easy to scan both across and down. Header words and body values remain intact.
critique.problems: The activity and conversion headers each run to four lines, leaving the shorter session header with unused space beneath it. The nearly equal widths do not fully reflect the different header lengths.
critique.cause: The activity column has 135px and the conversion column 136px, while the shorter session header also receives 135px.

critique.good: The wider activity column produces a compact, readable header, and the conversion header also groups its words reasonably well. Site rows remain clear.
critique.problems: The narrow support header stacks into five lines, including an isolated “of,” and dictates the height of the entire header row. The session header is also cramped.
critique.cause: The support column is only 92px and the session column 100px; much of the available width is concentrated in the 200px activity column.

critique.good: The conversion and support headers are compact, and their body values have generous space.
critique.problems: The activity header becomes a narrow six-line stack that dominates the table and creates considerable empty space under the other headers. The session header is also cramped, weakening the balance between related metrics.
critique.cause: The activity and session columns are only 105px and 100px, while conversion and support receive 175px and 162px.

critique.good: The site identifiers and values are easy to scan, and all four metric headers wrap at word boundaries. The widths give the long activity and conversion headers more room than the shorter duration header.
critique.problems: The header row feels uneven: duration and conversion each occupy four short lines, while the support header occupies three. The body values have considerably more room than they need.
critique.cause: The 115px duration column and 145px conversion column leave too little text width for longer phrases to stay together.

critique.good: The wider activity column gives its header a compact three-line shape, and the numeric columns remain easy to compare down the table.
critique.problems: The narrow support header breaks into four lines, including a line containing only “tickets.” Duration and conversion also remain four lines tall, making the header row feel fragmented.
critique.cause: Giving activity 170px leaves only 110px for duration, 140px for conversion and 122px for support.

critique.good: The conversion header reads in three coherent lines, and the support header also fits in three. The body rows retain a clear site-by-site rhythm.
critique.problems: Activity and duration remain four lines tall, with several short lines. The generous conversion width improves that header but leaves the neighboring activity header more compressed.
critique.cause: The 160px conversion column takes space from the 145px activity and 110px duration columns.

critique.good: The activity header reads in three balanced lines, and the site labels and values are easy to scan across each row and down each metric.
critique.problems: The session header is broken into four short lines, making it harder to read as a phrase. The purchase and support headers also occupy four lines, leaving a tall header above very short values.
critique.cause: At 115px, the session column cannot keep “session length” together. The 145px purchase column and 122px support column also force several short lines.

critique.good: The purchase header reads more smoothly in three lines, and its wider column gives the conversion metric a clear presence.
critique.problems: The activity header now ends with the isolated word “platforms,” while the session header remains fragmented into four lines. The header row stays just as tall as in r2A.
critique.cause: Moving 10px from activity to purchase reduces the activity column to 150px while leaving the session column at 115px and support at 122px.

critique.good: The session header improves markedly: “session length” stays together and the phrase fits in three lines. The site rows remain compact and easy to compare.
critique.problems: The activity header still leaves “platforms” alone on its last line, and the purchase header returns to four lines. The four-line support header continues to set the row height.
critique.cause: The 130px session column gains its space from activity and purchase, which are reduced to 150px and 140px respectively; support remains at 122px.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

ref_equal.why: All text stays intact and the rows scan clearly, but Site takes as much width as the metric columns despite containing single letters. The long headers consequently wrap into four lines.

r1B.why: The narrow Site column gives the long active-users header room to read in three lines. The other headers remain intact, though the median and ticket headers are somewhat cramped.

ref_auto.why: The columns fit their contents without breaking words, and the four-line headers have a consistent rhythm. The active-users header wraps a little more than necessary.

r3A.why: Space shifts from the short Site labels to the longer metric headers. The first two metrics read in three lines, while the others remain clear in four; the numeric rows are easy to compare.

contrast.why: The median and support-ticket columns are so narrow that words break across lines and even into isolated letters. The very tall header makes the table difficult to scan.

r1A.why: All words stay intact, and the support-ticket header gains a readable three-line wrap. The active-users and median headers are tighter, but the rows remain clear.

raw.unsure: B and F are also workable; the preference among them and D depends partly on which metric headers readers need to scan most often.

r1B.why: All words remain intact and the headers are readable, though the first metric has more space than it needs while the last two headers stack over four lines.

ref_equal.why: The headers remain intact, but the wide Site column leaves unnecessary space and makes the metric columns feel cramped.

r1A.why: The narrow Site column leaves useful room for the metrics, and the support header fits in three lines; the other long headers still stack over four.

ref_auto.why: The columns are reasonably balanced and all words remain intact, although all four metric headers occupy four lines.

r3A.why: The compact Site column gives room to the metrics; the first two metric headers fit comfortably in three lines, and all words remain intact.

contrast.why: The narrow session-length and support columns break words into fragments, making the headers difficult to read and creating an excessively tall header row.

raw.unsure: C is also well balanced; the preference for E rests on its more readable session-length header and overall distribution of space.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
